long_biography.plain_text:
Des Moines shaped Jay Bradley Levitt's early life before he graduated from the University of Iowa and moved west to San Diego. Work in hospitality and property management preceded a shift into entrepreneurship. From the early 1990s, he developed businesses in wireless communications and residential mortgages, repeatedly looking for simpler ways to reach customers.

A frustrating personal experience with conventional sleep-apnoea care later drew Levitt into healthcare. He launched Lofta in 2016, turning that insight into a company centred on convenience and continuity for patients. The business grew under his leadership and was sold to Apria five years later. Beyond commerce, Levitt became an early Curebound board member and joined its Founders Fund Circle, backing collaborative cancer research in San Diego. He died the following year.
